A1_C2.name: FDB-like procedure, formula UNVERIFIED (not attributed to any paper)
A1_C2.status: UNVERIFIED. Derived from Beran's double-bootstrap logic and a search-tool recollection; the original paper has NOT been read. It must not be attributed to Davidson and MacKinnon or to any paper until verified.
A1_C2.definition: outer B=999 day-resamples give T*_b; one inner day-resample of each outer sample gives T**_b; p1 = mean(T* >= T); Q = (1 - p1) quantile of {T**_b}; p_fdb = mean(T*_b > Q); reject iff p_fdb <= alpha
A1_C2.v1_defect: v1 computed mean(T** > Q), which equals p1 up to rounding (300 of 300 datasets, max difference 0.0000). v1 code and text are left unchanged.

per_cell.inputs: k rejections in n valid simulations; p_hat = k/n; Wilson 95% interval [L, U] (z = 1.959964)
per_cell.point_pass: v1 rule: lo <= p_hat <= hi, and (tier A/B) U <= Wilson limit, and p_hat <= 0.07; for C3 only p_hat <= hi
per_cell.ambiguous: a point-rule bound that applies (lo and hi; hi only for C3) satisfies L <= bound <= U
per_cell.status: PASS | PASS_AMBIGUOUS | FAIL | FAIL_AMBIGUOUS = point_pass x ambiguous

per_candidate.FAIL: at least one gated cell is FAIL
per_candidate.FAIL_BOUNDARY_ONLY: no FAIL, at least one FAIL_AMBIGUOUS; decision stays 'not selected'
per_candidate.MARGINAL_NOT_DEMONSTRATED: every gated cell point-passes, at least one is PASS_AMBIGUOUS; no claim of calibration is made

replication_rule.who_decides: only with the user's explicit approval; never automatic
replication_rule.what: the ambiguous cells only, 100,000 simulations, fresh seed (name ambiguity_replication, 20261210), same data process and method
replication_rule.decision: the point rule on the replication estimate ALONE (original estimate discarded, no pooling, to avoid optional stopping)
replication_rule.after: still ambiguous at n=100,000 -> final status MARGINAL_NOT_DEMONSTRATED; no further replication

A3_redundant_clauses.statement: At 25,000 simulations per gated cell the Wilson-upper clause and the 7.0% ceiling never change a decision. Checked exhaustively at n = 10,000, 20,000, 25,000, 50,000 and 100,000 (all redundant). At n = 1,000, 2,000 and 5,000 the Wilson clause DOES change 8-12 decisions per tier; a 500-step scan finds it first redundant at n = 8,500 (tier A) and 9,500 (tier B). The 7.0% ceiling changed no decision at any n tested. Redundancy is not claimed for untested n.
A3_redundant_clauses.evidence: gate_redundancy_check.csv: exhaustive over every k = 0..n, decisions with and without the clauses are identical
A3_redundant_clauses.why: tier A: p_hat <= 0.055 implies Wilson U <= 0.058 < 0.060; tier B: p_hat <= 0.060 implies U <= 0.063 < 0.065; both p_hat bounds are below 0.07
A3_redundant_clauses.consequence: the clauses stay in the spec text (harmless) but give no extra protection when a cell has at least 10,000 valid simulations; removing them would not change any decision at n = 25,000
A3_redundant_clauses.caveat: the Wilson clause binds when a cell has fewer than about 10,000 valid simulations (e.g. after numerical failures in a reduced cell or in tier C-sized cells)

A4_alternative_processes.common: 3 stocks, shape E, 59 days, NSE and US, 25,000 simulations, H0 true by construction, day factor f ~ N(0, 0.3^2) unless stated, unit-variance shocks
A4_alternative_processes.null_check: analytic E[(shock part)^2] = 1 within 1e-9 (tests) for a, b, e, f; unit-variance multipliers for c, d; THEN a Monte-Carlo period-mean check within 0.5% at 10^6 bars before use (Stage 4)
A4_alternative_processes.DEVIATION_e: process e: v1 / docs/15 wording (log day scale Student-t(3)) has infinite E[exp(2f)] (a t variable has no moment-generating function), so the expected squared return and the estimand do not exist. v1.1 uses a Gaussian scale mixture (5% of days with 3x the sd), overall sd 0.3. A5_C3_intermediate_sizes.training_family_per_size: tails G, T6, T4 x shapes E, D5 x markets NSE, US = 12 cells (the same family used for 125 and 250 days)
A5_C3_intermediate_sizes.rule: crit_n = max over the 12 training cells of size n of the 0.95 quantile of T (no margin); reject when T > crit_n
A5_C3_intermediate_sizes.applies_to: validation cells T7 and T5 (shape E) at 90 and 180 days; the 59-day cells use crit_59 from the 44-cell development family
A5_C3_intermediate_sizes.limitation: the family at 90 and 180 days has 12 cells (no estimated-dependence cells, no 0.6 day-volatility cells, no flat or R2 shapes), like 125 and 250 days; C3 is therefore less conservative there than at 59 days and is valid only inside that family
A5_C3_intermediate_sizes.cost_note: generation of the data only (benchmark / 4x speed-up); computing T adds a small amount; it is NOT part of the earlier resource table
